items.title: Bounded no-slip solenoidal closure spaces
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded open set. Let
$C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ denote smooth compactly supported vector
fields and set
$$D_\sigma(\Omega)=\{a\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{div}a=0\}.$$
Let $H$ be the closure of $D_\sigma(\Omega)$ in
$L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and let $V$ be its closure in
$H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where $H_0^1$ is the $H^1$ closure of
$C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ and weak derivatives define the $H^1$
norm. Use $\|a\|_H=\|a\|_2$ and
$\|a\|_V^2=\|a\|_2^2+\|\nabla a\|_2^2$. Each $V$ element has zero
extension in $H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ and distributional divergence zero. This
closure definition does not identify $V$ with every divergence-free member
of $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ on an arbitrary open set, and it makes no
pointwise boundary trace assertion.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §§2.1–2.2, printed pp. 4–5; their domains have additional boundary regularity.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §5.2, printed pp. 39–43, for the divergence-free energy-space convention.

items.title: Periodic solenoidal Fourier spaces
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ be an integer, and let $L>0$ be the numerical period in a fixed
length unit. Let
$\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$ carry normalized Lebesgue measure
$L^{-d}dx$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^d$ put
$\kappa_k=2\pi k/L$ and $e_k(x)=\exp(i\kappa_k\cdot x)$. For a complex
scalar or vector $L^2$ class $f$, let
$\widehat f(k)=L^{-d}\int_{[0,L]^d}f(x)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\,dx$;
real fields are the classes satisfying
$\widehat f(-k)=\overline{\widehat f(k)}$. Define
$H^s(\mathbb T_L^d)$ by
$$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}(1+L^2|\kappa_k|^2)^s|\widehat f(k)|^2<\infty,$$
for $s\ge0$, with the square root of this sum as norm; the weight is dimensionless. The
real solenoidal spaces are
$$H=\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^d): k\cdot\widehat u(k)=0\text{ for every }k\ne0\},\qquad V=H\cap H^1(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^d).$$
The zero Fourier mode is unrestricted. The orthogonal solenoidal projection
$P$ has multiplier $P_0=I$ and
$P_k=I-\kappa_k\kappa_k^{\mathsf T}/|\kappa_k|^2$ for $k\ne0$; the
for integer $N\ge0$, rectangular truncation $\Pi_N$ keeps precisely $|k|_\infty\le N$. A weak
derivative in coordinate $j$ has Fourier coefficient $i\kappa_{k,j}\widehat f(k)$.
For $r>0$, $H^{-r}$ is the completion of finite Fourier coefficient sequences
in the norm squared $\sum_k(1+L^2|\kappa_k|^2)^{-r}|\widehat f(k)|^2$.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §5.2.2, printed pp. 42–43; the local statement retains the mean mode.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §2.1–2.2, printed pp. 4–5; their solenoidal space is mean zero.

items.title: Weak time continuity and energy spaces
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $H,V,H^{-r}$ be the spaces of Periodic solenoidal Fourier spaces, let
$T>0$, and identify time-dependent functions that agree almost everywhere.
A map $u:[0,T]\to H$ is in $C_w([0,T];H)$ when
$t\mapsto (u(t),h)_H$ is continuous for each fixed $h\in H$. A map
$u:(0,T)\to X$ into a separable Hilbert space $X$ is strongly measurable
when it is an almost-everywhere pointwise limit of measurable simple
$X$-valued maps. For $1\le p<\infty$, $L^p(0,T;X)$ consists of strongly
measurable maps with $\int_0^T\|u(t)\|_X^pdt<\infty$; $L^\infty(0,T;X)$
uses the essential supremum norm. In this page, $L^p_{\rm loc}(0,\infty;X)$
means membership on every finite interval $(0,T)$. These conventions also
apply with $X=V$ and $X=H^{-r}$.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §5.5, printed p. 48.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)

items.title: Countable smooth solenoidal basis for bounded closure spaces
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every nonempty bounded open
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, the closure spaces $H,V$ of
Bounded no-slip solenoidal closure spaces are separable Hilbert spaces, with
$V\hookrightarrow H$ continuous and dense. There is a countable sequence
$e_j\in D_\sigma(\Omega)$ that is orthonormal in $H$ and whose finite linear
span is dense in both $H$ and $V$. No Stokes eigenfunction regularity or
identification of $V$ with a larger solenoidal space is asserted.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §§2.1–2.2 and §5.2, printed pp. 4–5 and 14–15; the proof here constructs the basis from the closure spaces.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §5.2, printed pp. 39–43, for the periodic Fourier separability input.

items.title: Quadratic transport in negative Sobolev space
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $L>0$, $r>d/2+1$, and $a\in L^2(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^d)$.
For the Fourier projection $P$ and divergence convention of
Periodic solenoidal Fourier spaces, the distribution $P\operatorname{div}(a\otimes a)$ belongs to $H^{-r}$ and satisfies
$$\|P\operatorname{div}(a\otimes a)\|_{H^{-r}}\le C(d,L,r)\|a\|_2^2.$$
Here $(a\otimes a)_{ij}=a_i a_j$ and
$(\operatorname{div}A)_i=\sum_j\partial_jA_{ij}$. The estimate uses no
three-dimensional singular-integral bound.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §5.3.2, printed pp. 44–46; this proof uses a direct Fourier estimate.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §4, printed pp. 8–12; this proof does not import its abstract compactness step.

items.title: Unforced periodic Leray–Hopf solution
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $L>0$, $\nu>0$, $u_0\in H$, and use the spaces and weak-time
conventions of Periodic solenoidal Fourier spaces and
Weak time continuity and energy spaces. A **global unforced periodic Leray–Hopf
solution** with data $(\nu,u_0)$ is a map
$u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\rm loc}(0,\infty;V)$
such that $u(0)=u_0$ in $H$, $\|u(t)-u_0\|_H\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$, and for
every smooth real periodic divergence-free test field
$\phi:[0,\infty)\times\mathbb T_L^d\to\mathbb R^d$ compactly supported in
time,
$$\int_0^\infty\!\big[(u,\partial_t\phi)+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)\big]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))=0.$$
It must also satisfy, for every $t\ge0$,
$$\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2,$$
and there must be a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for
every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and every $t\ge s$,
$$\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.$$
For a matrix field $A$, $(\operatorname{div}A)_i=\sum_j\partial_jA_{ij}$. The tensor pairing means $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$;
the gradient pairing means $\nabla u:\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i$.
All derivatives in the weak identity are distributional; the definition
asserts neither uniqueness nor smoothness.

references.locator: §5.5, printed pp. 48–49.

items.title: No-slip compactness and bounded-mode tails
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and open, and let $H,V$ and
$(e_j)_{j\ge1}$ be as in the bounded closure-space and basis results on this
page. The inclusion $V\hookrightarrow H$ is compact. If $\Pi_K$ is the
$H$-orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(e_1,\ldots,e_K)$, then
there are numbers $\delta_K\downarrow0$ such that
$$\|(I-\Pi_K)a\|_H\le\delta_K\|a\|_V\qquad(a\in V).$$

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §4, printed pp. 8–12; the local proof uses zero extension and mollification.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §§5.3–5.4, printed pp. 43–48; the local bounded-domain proof is independent.

items.title: Separability and Hilbert structure of the no-slip dual
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and let $V$ be the separable real Hilbert space supplied by the bounded solenoidal basis
result above. Its continuous real-linear dual $V^*$,
with norm $\|\ell\|_{V^*}=\sup_{\|v\|_V\le1}|\ell(v)|$, is a separable real
Hilbert space. The Riesz map
$$J:V\to V^*,\qquad Jw(v)=(w,v)_V$$
is a surjective linear isometry.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §2.2, printed pp. 4–5, for the Hilbert structures on the divergence-free energy spaces.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §§5.2.2–5.4, printed pp. 42–48, for the periodic Hilbert-space and compactness framework.

items.title: Fourier compactness with coefficient time control
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $L>0$, and $T>0$. Let $z_n:[0,T]\to H$ be continuous
finite-Fourier-sum curves such that, for constants $A,B<\infty$,
$$\sup_{n,t}\|z_n(t)\|_H\le A,\qquad \sup_n\int_0^T\|\nabla z_n(t)\|_2^2dt\le B,$$
and for each $k\in\mathbb Z^d$ there is $C_k<\infty$ with
$|\widehat z_n(k,t)-\widehat z_n(k,s)|\le C_k|t-s|$ for all $n,s,t$.
Then some subsequence converges uniformly in each Fourier coefficient to
$z\in C_w([0,T];H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$, with
$\sup_t\|z(t)\|_H\le A$ and $\int_0^T\|\nabla z\|_2^2dt\le B$; it also
converges strongly to $z$ in $L^2(0,T;H)$ and, after a further subsequence,
strongly in $H$ for almost every $t$.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §§5.3–5.4, printed pp. 43–48; the present proof uses explicit Fourier tails.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §4, printed pp. 8–12; the present proof supplies finite-mode tails directly.

items.title: Elementary zero-boundary L6 and L4 interpolation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and
open, and let $H,V$ be the closure spaces defined above. There is a constant $C$ independent of $\Omega$
and $a$ such that every $a\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies
$$\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla a\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|a\|_{L^4(\Omega)}\le\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^{1/4}\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}^{3/4}.$$
For $T>0$, if $u\in L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$, then
$u\in L^{8/3}(0,T;L^4(\Omega))$. Here the time-dependent $L^p$ notation
means strong measurability and integrability of the displayed norm; the
continuous embedding $V\to L^4(\Omega)$ carries strongly measurable
$V$-valued maps to strongly measurable $L^4$-valued maps. Let $V^*$ be the
continuous real-linear dual of $V$ with its operator norm and set
$$b_u(t)(\phi)=-\int_\Omega u_i(t,x)u_j(t,x)\partial_j\phi_i(x)dx,\qquad\phi\in V.$$
Then $b_u(t)\in V^*$, $t\mapsto b_u(t)$ is strongly measurable, and
$b_u\in L^{4/3}(0,T;V^*)$ with
$\|b_u(t)\|_{V^*}\le\|u(t)\|_{L^4(\Omega)}^2.$

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §2.2, printed p. 5, inequality (4); the local proof derives the estimate directly.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024

items.title: Global periodic weak viscous existence
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $L>0$, $\nu>0$, and $u_0\in H$ for the periodic solenoidal
Fourier spaces defined above. Assume the finite-dimensional ODE principle that on a closed cylinder where
$\|F\|\le B$ and $F$ is $L$-Lipschitz in the state, the integral map on
curves within radius $r$ of the initial state is invariant when $hB\le r$ and
a contraction when $hL<1$. Then there
exists a global unforced periodic Leray–Hopf solution with data $(\nu,u_0)$
under the definition above. This is an existence assertion; it asserts no
uniqueness or global smoothness.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: Theorem 5.9 and proof, §§5.2–5.5, printed pp. 39–51; the local proof retains the mean mode and proves finite-mode compactness directly.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: Theorem 3 and proof, §5.2, printed pp. 14–15, flat-torus case.

items.title: Mean-zero pressure as a distribution
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $u$ be a solution supplied by
Global periodic weak viscous existence on $\mathbb T_L^d$, with $d\ge2$,
$L>0$, and viscosity $\nu>0$. Then there is a unique mean-zero-in-space
distribution $\pi$ on $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb T_L^d$ such that
$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u$
as a spacetime distribution, normalized by requiring its zero spatial Fourier
coefficient to vanish. No function-space or pointwise regularity for $\pi$ is
asserted.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §5.1, printed pp. 37–39; the local proof constructs pressure by Fourier coefficients.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: Lemma 2, §3, printed pp. 6–7, periodic case.

items.title: Global bounded no-slip Leray–Hopf existence
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and open, assume the Axiom of
Choice, let $\nu>0$, and let $u_0\in H$ for the bounded closure spaces
defined above. Assume the finite-dimensional ODE principle that on a closed cylinder where
$\|F\|\le B$ and $F$ is $L$-Lipschitz in the state, the integral map on
curves within radius $r$ of the initial state is invariant when $hB\le r$ and
a contraction when $hL<1$. There exists
$$u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\rm loc}(0,\infty;V)$$
with $u(0)=u_0$ and $\|u(t)-u_0\|_H\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$, satisfying for
every compactly time-supported $C^1$ map $\phi:[0,\infty)\to V$,
$$\int_0^\infty\!\big[(u,\partial_t\phi)+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)\big]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))=0.$$
It also satisfies
$$\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2\quad(t\ge0),$$
and there is a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every
$s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and $t\ge s$,
$$\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.$$
The conclusion is a velocity result for the specified unforced closure-space
formulation; it asserts no uniqueness, smoothness, pressure regularity, or
boundary trace beyond membership in $H_0^1$. Here
Here $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$ and
$\nabla u:\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i$. For a matrix field
$A$, $(\operatorname{div}A)_i=\sum_j\partial_jA_{ij}$.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: Theorem 3 and proof, §5.2, printed pp. 14–15; that source treats smoother domains, while this proof uses the closure spaces stated here.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §§5.2–5.5, printed pp. 39–51, for the Galerkin and energy framework.

items.title: Weak–smooth uniqueness on a smooth interval
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $u$ be a global unforced periodic Leray–Hopf solution on $\mathbb T_L^d$
with viscosity $\nu>0$ and initial datum $u_0$. Suppose
$v\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^d)$ and
$q\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\mathbb T_L^d)$ satisfy $\operatorname{div}v=0$ and
$\partial_tv+\operatorname{div}(v\otimes v)+\nabla q=\nu\Delta v$, with
$v(0)=u_0$. Then $u(t)=v(t)$ in $H$ for every $t\in[0,T]$. More generally,
for $D(t)=\|u(t)-v(t)\|_2^2$,
$$D(t)\le D(0)+2\int_0^t\|\nabla v(s)\|_\infty D(s)\,ds.$$
This conditional result does not assert existence of such a smooth pair.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §6.1, printed pp. 53–54; its theorem compares strong solutions, while the local proof treats a weak solution against a smooth one.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: Definition 1 in §3, printed p. 6, and §4, printed pp. 8–12, for the weak formulation and energy inequality.

items.title: Rectangular evolving distributional pressure
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(a_i,b_i)\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a finite open
rectangle, and let $u$ be the velocity supplied by the bounded no-slip weak
existence theorem on this page. Assume the rectangular divergence-inverse
result: there is a continuous linear map
$R:D_0(\Omega)\to C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where
$D_0(\Omega)=\{h\in C_c^\infty(\Omega):\int_\Omega h=0\}$, such that
$\operatorname{div}Rh=h$. For each compact $K\subset\Omega$ there is a compact
$K'\subset\Omega$ containing the support of $Rh$ whenever $h$ is supported in
$K$, and on each fixed-support test space $R$ is continuous for all seminorms
$\sup|\partial^\alpha h|$. Then there is a spacetime distribution $\pi$ with
$$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u$$
on $(0,\infty)\times\Omega$. Its normalization may be fixed by any
$\theta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\int_\Omega\theta=1$ through
$\langle\pi,a(t)\theta(x)\rangle=0$ for every compactly supported smooth
temporal test $a$. Pressure is unique under this normalization. This is a
conditional distributional statement and gives no $L^2$ pressure estimate,
corner regularity, or pointwise boundary traction. Here
$(u\otimes u):\nabla\psi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\psi_i$.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: Lemma 2, §3, printed pp. 6–7; the authors defer bounded-domain pressure recovery to other operator theory.

items.title: Weak convergence does not pass quadratic products
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
**False statement.** Weak convergence in the periodic solenoidal space $H$
alone guarantees weak convergence of the quadratic tensors $u_n\otimes u_n$
to $u\otimes u$.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §§5.3–5.4, printed pp. 43–48, for the need to control nonlinear products in compactness arguments.

references.title: L. C. Berselli and S. Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §4, printed pp. 8–12, for strong compactness in the passage to the nonlinear term.

items.title: Weak existence and smooth regularity scope
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
The periodic existence theorem gives a global weak solution for every stated
initial datum and positive viscosity, conditional on the finite-dimensional ODE
input stated in its theorem; it does not prove global smoothness or
uniqueness among all three-dimensional weak solutions. The weak–smooth theorem
only yields uniqueness on an interval where a smooth solution with the same
data is already given. The compactness argument uses a positive-viscosity
gradient bound; its proof does not apply at $\nu=0$. These are limits of the
claims proved on this page and are not assertions about empirical fluid
behavior.

references.title: Leonid Ryzhik, Math 256B Lecture Notes, version 2024
references.locator: §5.6, printed pp. 52–53; §6.1, printed pp. 53–54.

references.locator: §§3–5, printed pp. 5–16; the local remark is limited to its stated theorem scopes.
